question: One line has slope 2. Another line is perpendicular to it and has a defined slope. What is the slope of the other line?
solution: The product of the two slopes is \(-1\), so the slope of the other line is \(-1/2\).

edges.reason: The explicit criterion is division converted to multiplication by the divisor's reciprocal, so reciprocal meaning is indispensable to that procedure.
Knowing k in y=kx+b is customary preparation and connects slope to an earlier idea. Slope can still be defined from inclination without linear functions.
Slope is explicitly the tangent of the inclination angle.
Judging whether the lines are parallel requires the meaning of parallelism, which cnm_067 explicitly defines. Its parallel postulate and transitivity proof are outside this prerequisite scope.
